goal.sl: Poveš, kaj je bilo pred nečim v preteklosti (When we got there, the bus had gone), rabiš 'd, hadn't in by the time in veš, kdaj ostane past simple.
goal.de: Du sagst, was vor etwas in der Vergangenheit war (When we got there, the bus had gone), nimmst 'd, hadn't und by the time und weißt, wann das past simple bleibt.
goal.it: Dici ciò che è venuto prima di qualcosa nel passato (When we got there, the bus had gone), usi 'd, hadn't e by the time e sai quando resta il past simple.
goal.en: You can say what came before something in the past (When we got there, the bus had gone), use 'd, hadn't and by the time, and know when the past simple stays.

say.sl: **The bus had gone**: **had** + deležnik, kadar že govoriš o preteklosti in je nekaj bilo še prej. **When we got to the stop, the bus had already gone.** (Ko smo prišli na postajo, je avtobus že odpeljal.) Najprej avtobus, potem mi. Za vse osebe je enako had. Slovenščina reče tu preteklik in *že*.
say.de: **The bus had gone**: **had** + Partizip, wenn du schon von der Vergangenheit sprichst und etwas noch davor war. **When we got to the stop, the bus had already gone.** (Als wir zur Haltestelle kamen, war der Bus schon weg.) Zuerst der Bus, dann wir. Für alle Personen had, auch wo Deutsch *war gegangen* sagt.
say.it: **The bus had gone**: **had** + il participio, quando parli già del passato e qualcosa è venuto ancora prima. **When we got to the stop, the bus had already gone.** (Quando siamo arrivati alla fermata, l'autobus era già partito.) Prima l'autobus, poi noi. Per tutte le persone had, anche dove l'italiano dice *era partito*.
say.en: **The bus had gone**: **had** + the participle, when you are already talking about the past and something came earlier still. **When we got to the stop, the bus had already gone.** First the bus, then us. The same had for every person.

say.sl: **'d** je kratko za had: **She'd gone.** (Odšla je že.) Zanikano **hadn't**: **We hadn't eaten.** (Še nismo jedli.) Vprašanje: **Had you seen it before?** Pred deležnikom je 'd had, pred osnovno obliko would: **I'd like**. V pisanju je deležnik, **I'd gone**, čeprav nekateri rečejo *I'd went*.
say.de: **'d** ist kurz für had: **She'd gone.** (Sie war schon gegangen.) Verneint **hadn't**: **We hadn't eaten.** (Wir hatten nichts gegessen.) Frage: **Had you seen it before?** Vor dem Partizip ist 'd had, vor der Grundform would: **I'd like**. Geschrieben steht das Partizip, **I'd gone**, auch wenn manche *I'd went* sagen.
say.it: **'d** è la forma breve di had: **She'd gone.** (Se n'era andata.) Negativo **hadn't**: **We hadn't eaten.** (Non avevamo mangiato.) Domanda: **Had you seen it before?** Prima del participio 'd è had, prima della forma base would: **I'd like**. Per iscritto si usa il participio, **I'd gone**, anche se qualcuno dice *I'd went*.
say.en: **'d** is short for had: **She'd gone.** No: **hadn't**: **We hadn't eaten.** To ask: **Had you seen it before?** Before a participle 'd is had, before a base form would: **I'd like**. Writing wants the participle, **I'd gone**, though some people say *I'd went*.

say.sl: **By the time we got there, the bus had gone.** **by the time** + past simple, v drugem delu had: ko smo prišli, je bilo že. (Ko smo prišli, je avtobus že odpeljal.) Pogosto so zraven **already**, **just** in **never … before**: **I'd never seen the sea before.** (Morja še nikoli nisem videl{m:|f:a}.)
say.de: **By the time we got there, the bus had gone.** **by the time** + past simple, im anderen Teil had: Als wir kamen, war es schon so. (Als wir ankamen, war der Bus schon weg.) Oft dabei: **already**, **just** und **never … before**: **I'd never seen the sea before.** (Ich hatte das Meer noch nie gesehen.)
say.it: **By the time we got there, the bus had gone.** **by the time** + past simple, nell'altra parte had: quando siamo arrivati, era già così. (Quando siamo arrivati, l'autobus era già partito.) Spesso con **already**, **just** e **never … before**: **I'd never seen the sea before.** (Non avevo mai visto il mare.)
say.en: **By the time we got there, the bus had gone.** **by the time** + the past simple, had in the other half: when we came, it was already so. Often with **already**, **just** and **never … before**: **I'd never seen the sea before.**

say.sl: **When I got home, Sam left**: Sam je šel potem. **When I got home, Sam had left**: Sam je šel prej, nisem ga več {m:videl|f:videla}. Kar poveš po vrsti, ostane v past simple: **I got up, fed the dogs and left.** (Vstal{m:|f:a} sem, nahranil{m:|f:a} pse in {m:šel|f:šla}.) had je le za tisto, kar je zunaj vrste.
say.de: **When I got home, Sam left**: Sam ging danach. **When I got home, Sam had left**: Sam ging davor, ich habe ihn nicht mehr gesehen. Was der Reihe nach kommt, bleibt im past simple: **I got up, fed the dogs and left.** (Ich stand auf, fütterte die Hunde und ging.) had nur für das, was aus der Reihe fällt.
say.it: **When I got home, Sam left**: Sam è andato via dopo. **When I got home, Sam had left**: Sam è andato via prima, non l'ho più visto. Ciò che racconti in ordine resta al past simple: **I got up, fed the dogs and left.** (Mi sono alzat{m:o|f:a}, ho dato da mangiare ai cani e sono uscit{m:o|f:a}.) had solo per ciò che esce dall'ordine.
say.en: **When I got home, Sam left**: Sam went afterwards. **When I got home, Sam had left**: Sam went earlier, and I didn't see him. What you tell in order stays in the past simple: **I got up, fed the dogs and left.** had only for what falls out of the order.

say.sl: **After she had fed the hens, she went in**: z **after** in **before** je vrstni red že povedan, zato je prav tudi **After she fed the hens, she went in.** Pri **because** pa je vzrok pogosto prej: **He was tired because he hadn't slept.** (Bil je utrujen, ker ni spal.)
say.de: **After she had fed the hens, she went in**: Mit **after** und **before** ist die Reihenfolge schon gesagt, also stimmt auch **After she fed the hens, she went in.** Bei **because** liegt der Grund oft davor: **He was tired because he hadn't slept.** (Er war müde, weil er nicht geschlafen hatte.)
say.it: **After she had fed the hens, she went in**: con **after** e **before** l'ordine è già detto, quindi va bene anche **After she fed the hens, she went in.** Con **because** la causa spesso viene prima: **He was tired because he hadn't slept.** (Era stanco perché non aveva dormito.)
say.en: **After she had fed the hens, she went in**: with **after** and **before** the order is already said, so **After she fed the hens, she went in** is right too. With **because** the reason often came first: **He was tired because he hadn't slept.**

exercises.text: Yesterday was a bad day for Jack. When he got up, Meg ___ (go). She ___ (run) after the sheep in the night. By the time he found her, it ___ (start) to rain. He got to the farm at ten, but he ___ (not have) breakfast, and he ___ (forget) his coat. He went to the Packhorse Inn, but Mrs Birkett ___ (close) the kitchen. He'd never ___ (be) so hungry!

translation.sl: Včeraj je imel Jack slab dan. Ko je vstal, je Meg že ni bilo. Ponoči je stekla za ovcami. Ko jo je našel, je že začelo deževati. Na kmetijo je prišel ob desetih, a ni zajtrkoval in je pozabil plašč. Šel je v gostilno Packhorse, a gospa Birkett je že zaprla kuhinjo. Še nikoli ni bil tako lačen!
translation.de: Gestern war ein schlechter Tag für Jack. Als er aufstand, war Meg schon weg. Sie war in der Nacht den Schafen nachgelaufen. Als er sie fand, hatte es schon zu regnen begonnen. Er kam um zehn zum Hof, aber er hatte nicht gefrühstückt und seinen Mantel vergessen. Er ging ins Packhorse Inn, aber Mrs Birkett hatte die Küche schon zugesperrt. Er war noch nie so hungrig gewesen!
translation.it: Ieri è stata una brutta giornata per Jack. Quando si è alzato, Meg se n'era andata. Era corsa dietro alle pecore durante la notte. Quando l'ha trovata, aveva già cominciato a piovere. È arrivato alla fattoria alle dieci, ma non aveva fatto colazione e aveva dimenticato il cappotto. È andato alla Packhorse Inn, ma Mrs Birkett aveva già chiuso la cucina. Non aveva mai avuto tanta fame!
translation.en: Yesterday was a bad day for Jack. When he got up, Meg had gone. She had run after the sheep in the night. By the time he found her, it had started to rain. He got to the farm at ten, but he hadn't had breakfast, and he had forgotten his coat. He went to the Packhorse Inn, but Mrs Birkett had closed the kitchen. He'd never been so hungry!

exercises.text: When Mr Dixon came to the smithy, somebody ___ (take) his hammer. By the time he found it, the fire ___ (go) out. He'd ___ (leave) the door open. He ___ (not lock) it, and now he was angry. — I'd never ___ (see) him so angry!

translation.sl: Ko je gospod Dixon prišel v kovačnico, mu je nekdo vzel kladivo. Ko ga je našel, je ogenj že ugasnil. Pustil je odprta vrata. Ni jih zaklenil in zdaj je bil jezen. — Še nikoli ga nisem videl{m:|f:a} tako jeznega!
translation.de: Als Mr Dixon in die Schmiede kam, hatte jemand seinen Hammer genommen. Als er ihn fand, war das Feuer schon aus. Er hatte die Tür offen gelassen. Er hatte sie nicht zugesperrt, und jetzt war er böse. — Ich hatte ihn noch nie so böse gesehen!
translation.it: Quando Mr Dixon è arrivato alla fucina, qualcuno aveva preso il suo martello. Quando l'ha trovato, il fuoco si era già spento. Aveva lasciato la porta aperta. Non l'aveva chiusa a chiave, e ora era arrabbiato. — Non l'avevo mai visto così arrabbiato!
translation.en: When Mr Dixon came to the smithy, somebody had taken his hammer. By the time he found it, the fire had gone out. He'd left the door open. He hadn't locked it, and now he was angry. — I'd never seen him so angry!
